items.stem: The first stage of a predictive analytics project is best described as:

options.text: Defining the business problem and success criteria
options.rationale: Correct: a clear problem definition guides all later modelling.

options.text: Deploying the final model to production
options.rationale: Deployment is a late stage, not the first.
Tuning comes after data and modelling steps begin.
Reporting is near the end of the project.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear problem definition guides all later modelling.

items.stem: Why split data into training and validation sets?

options.text: To estimate how the model generalizes to unseen data
options.rationale: Correct: validation data gives an unbiased estimate of generalization.

options.text: To make the model train faster
options.rationale: Splitting is about validity, not speed.

options.text: Because regulators forbid using all the data
options.rationale: That is not the reason for a train/validation split.

options.text: To guarantee the model has zero error

items.explanation: Correct: validation data gives an unbiased estimate of generalization.

items.stem: Select TWO good practices when preparing data for modelling.

options.text: Investigating and handling missing values deliberately
options.rationale: Correct: missing-data handling affects model quality and must be deliberate.

options.text: Checking for and addressing obvious data-entry errors
options.rationale: Correct: cleaning erroneous values improves model reliability.

options.text: Deleting any variable you do not personally like
options.rationale: Variable selection should be evidence-based, not arbitrary.

options.text: Leaking the target variable into the predictors
Rounding all numbers to whole integers to simplify
options.rationale: Arbitrary rounding can destroy useful signal.

items.explanation: Correct: missing-data handling affects model quality and must be deliberate.
